A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhyGDPO work and contain 17 readable pages, including the complete appendix proof. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching research content; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, a 104-participant user study, component ablations, and hyperparameter analyses in Section 3 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, 104-participant user study, ablations, and hyperparameter results in Section 3 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the identical PhyAugPipe pipeline, groupwise preference objective, Physics-Guided Rewarding, and LoRA-Switch Reference procedure. No algorithm, architecture, loss, or inference change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions retain PhyVidGen-135K training data, VideoPhy2 and PhyGenBench evaluation, and the same additional action examples. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within every comparison in Tables 1–2 and the qualitative figures, including VideoDPO, PhyT2V, Flow-DPO, and the foundation-model baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3 retains the same data selection, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training settings, and user-study procedures. The study still reports 104 participants completing 48 trials each.

E4.justification: The component and LoRA-SR ablations, cross-evaluator and cross-model evaluations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, and visual analyses in Tables 2–3 and Figures 7–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report user-study 95% confidence intervals no wider than ±2.4%. Random-seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are otherwise identical.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports PhyGDPO's VideoPhy2 overall score as 0.1627 and PhyGenBench average as 0.55 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), their assumptions and derivations, and the complete appendix proof in Equations (15)–(27) are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about physics consistency, groupwise optimization, training efficiency, benchmark performance, and human preference.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component effectiveness and generalization, discussion of imperfect VLM evaluation, and arguments about real-video supervision are unchanged. No new applicability boundary or limitation is stated.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, and the project-page link are unchanged. The updated arXiv self-link merely identifies v4 and adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 4, all 78 references, and the positioning relative to prompt-extension and preference-optimization methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv:2512.24551v3 dated 5 March 2026 to v4 dated 18 June 2026. This is a minor header-text update; manuscript wording and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–3, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages match exactly outside the first-page version/date stamp accounted for under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only the arXiv version/date stamp and its self-link. The scientific content, empirical evidence, appendix proof, reproducibility details, and substantive presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
